content:
Meta continues to take its AI technology seriously. The latest sign? A Mac app dedicated to Meta AI.

Meta joins the fiercely competitive Mac AI app market

The brand-new Meta AI desktop app launches as version 1.0 beta, taking up just 16MB after installation.

Based on an initial inspection, the app runs natively on Macs equipped with Apple Silicon and macOS 15 or later, using the AppKit and SwiftUI frameworks alongside WebKit to deliver richer chat content. In other words, it is not an Electron app, nor is it a repackaged iPad version.

It includes Mac-specific integrations that make the desktop experience more complete than the Meta AI mobile app.

Quick Invoke uses an Option-Space shortcut to pop up a streamlined Meta AI writing window while you're working on anything. Another voice input feature lets you hold a shortcut to speak, then converts your voice into text for input into any app — whether it's email, documents, or a code editor.

Meta AI can also attach another Mac window to a conversation. With screen recording and accessibility permissions, the app can read the visible text in the window and take a screenshot for your next prompt. For now, this is just about gathering context, not computer control.

In addition to chat, the sidebar includes media, Artifacts, scheduled tasks, conversation history, and a personalised "About Me" section.

Users can switch between different thinking modes, attach files, generate media, and set up recurring information summaries or reminders. The app can also hide the Dock icon for users who prefer to summon it via keyboard shortcuts.

Meta's recent AI offensive

The Mac app is the latest in a string of new product releases. Back in April, Meta replaced Llama with Muse Spark. Updates in May further expanded Meta AI with more natural voice conversations and real-time camera-based assistance.

In July, image generation powered by Muse came to Meta AI, WhatsApp, and Instagram — though Meta subsequently removed a feature that generated images based on public Instagram posts. Meta AI also moved into Threads DMs to offer private chat services.

More recently, Meta launched Muse Code, a terminal-based AI coding agent for macOS and Linux.
